title: Baldur's Gate
wiki_lead:
Baldur's Gate is a series of role-playing video games set in the Forgotten Realms Dungeons & Dragons campaign setting. The series has been divided into two sub-series, known as the Bhaalspawn Saga and the Dark Alliance, both taking place mostly within the Western Heartlands, but the Bhaalspawn Saga extends to Amn and Tethyr. The Dark Alliance series was released for consoles and was critically and commercially successful. The Bhaalspawn Saga was critically acclaimed for using pausable real-time gameplay, which is credited with revitalizing the computer role-playing game (CRPG) genre.
The Bhaalspawn Saga was originally developed by BioWare for personal computers. Beamdog and its division Overhaul Games developed remakes of the original games in HD. The Dark Alliance series was originally set to be developed by Snowblind Studios, but ports were handled by Black Isle Studios, High Voltage Software, and Magic Pockets, with the second game developed by Black Isle.
Black Isle Studios had planned a third series to be set in the Dalelands and be a PC-exclusive hack and slash game with pausable real-time gameplay. The game would not have been connected to the Bhaalspawn Saga series. The game was cancelled when Interplay forfeited the D&D PC license to Atari.
The series was revived in 2012 with Baldur's Gate: Enhanced Edition, an update of the original Baldur's Gate using an enhanced Infinity Engine. The release of the Enhanced Edition marked the first release in the series in eight years, and was followed by a revival of the second Baldur's Gate called Baldur's Gate II: Enhanced Edition. Beamdog was granted permission to develop new games with the license, such as Baldur's Gate: Siege of Dragonspear, an expansion for Baldur's Gate: Enhanced Edition. The license was later given to Larian Studios, who developed and published Baldur's Gate 3, released in 2023.

Games

The Baldur's Gate series brought technical advancements over role-playing video games of the past. BioWare's Infinity Engine offers a pre-rendered isometric worldview, with sprite-based characters. Baldur's Gate was the third computer game to make use of the Lua scripting language. The engine was used for Planescape: Torment and the Icewind Dale series.
The earliest released in the series are based on a real-time modification of the second edition AD&D (Advanced Dungeons & Dragons) ruleset. The player's party can have up to six members, either created by the player according to the AD&D rules or non-player characters (NPCs) recruited by the protagonist from the game world. 
Baldur's Gate 3 is based on Dungeons & Dragons 5th Edition, and the party is limited to 4 characters.
Numerous side quests and plot twists are associated with particular NPCs and can be activated if they are found in the player's party. Through extensive, context-dependent dialogue, many characters inside and outside the player's party are fleshed out and given an added level of complexity.

grok_lead: Baldur's Gate is a renowned series of role-playing video games (RPGs) set in the Forgotten Realms campaign setting of the Dungeons & Dragons (D&D) tabletop RPG, developed primarily by BioWare and Larian Studios, and known for its deep storytelling, party-based gameplay, and adaptation of D&D rules into digital form. The series originated with the 1998 release of Baldur's Gate, developed by BioWare and published by Interplay Productions, which introduced the Bhaalspawn Sagaâa narrative centered on the protagonist's divine heritage as a child of the dead god Bhaalâand utilized the Infinity Engine for real-time with pause combat mechanics inspired by Advanced Dungeons & Dragons 2nd Edition rules. This game follows the player's character, an orphan from Candlekeep, as they investigate iron shortages and a cult threat along the Sword Coast, recruiting companions like the ranger Minsc and druid Jaheira while exploring a vast world of forests, cities, and dungeons. An expansion, Tales of the Sword Coast, followed in 1999, adding new quests and areas such as the pirate-infested Werewood and the haunted island of Durlag's Tower. The saga continued with Baldur's Gate II: Shadows of Amn in 2000, again developed by BioWare and published by Interplay, shifting the story to the city of Athkatla where the protagonist seeks to rescue their sister Imoen from the mage Jon Irenicus, delving into themes of identity, betrayal, and power with expanded companion interactions and moral choices. The 2001 expansion Throne of Bhaal concluded the Bhaalspawn storyline, featuring epic confrontations in the hellish realms and the throne room of Bhaal himself, effectively replacing a planned third mainline game due to development constraints. Spin-off titles include Baldur's Gate: Dark Alliance (2001), an action RPG developed by Snowblind Studios and published by Interplay for consoles, focusing on hack-and-slash dungeon crawling with co-op play and minimal narrative, set in Baldur's Gate during the iron crisis. Its sequel, Baldur's Gate: Dark Alliance II (2004), expanded the formula with five playable characters and larger environments. In the 2010s, Beamdog released enhanced editions of the original games and expansions (2012â2013), updating the titles for modern platforms with improved graphics, widescreen support, additional quests, and new companions like the monk Rasaad yn Bashir, while preserving the core Infinity Engine experience. These editions revitalized interest in the series, introducing Siege of Dragonspear (2016), an original story bridging the first and second games, set during a crusader invasion of the Sword Coast. The series reached new heights with Baldur's Gate III in 2023, developed and published by Larian Studios (creators of Divinity: Original Sin 2), which adapts D&D 5th Edition rules in a turn-based combat system and follows a diverse party of adventurers infected by mind flayer tadpoles, journeying from the Sword Coast to the hells of Avernus amid a cult's machinations. Set over a century after the previous games in 1492 DR, it emphasizes player-driven narratives, cooperative multiplayer for up to four players, and extensive character customization across races like elves and tieflings and classes such as wizards and rogues. Throughout its history, the Baldur's Gate series has profoundly influenced the CRPG genre by blending tactical combat, branching narratives, and D&D lore, establishing BioWare's reputation for character-focused storytelling that carried into titles like Mass Effect, and inspiring a resurgence of isometric RPGs in the 2010s and 2020s. Baldur's Gate III in particular garnered over 200 Game of the Year awards, including major honors from BAFTA, underscoring the franchise's enduring legacy in bridging tabletop and video game RPGs.
